content.text:
I have what I need. The agreement is engagement-by-engagement with no volume or spend commitment:

- **§1(a)/(b)**: Services are retained "on a task by task basis," defined only through mutually agreed Statements of Work.
- **§3(a)/(b)**: Compensation is "on a time and materials" basis "as set forth in each Statement of Work" — no retainer, minimum hours, or guaranteed spend.
- **§6(b)**: On termination, Contractor is paid only "all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned... through the effective date" — a true-up, not a shortfall penalty or acceleration.

Searches for "minimum," "commit," "shortfall," "take or pay," "retainer," "non-refundable," and "prepaid" returned no commitment language anywhere in the document. No volume caps on our usage either. This meets the preferred position, so no redline is warranted.

input.quote: (a) During the term of this Agreement, Company agrees to compensate Contractor as set forth in each Statement of Work. Contractor will be compensated on a time and materials.
input.rationale: No minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall charge, or volume restriction on Customer appears in the Agreement. Services are engaged "on a task by task basis" under mutually agreed Statements of Work (§1(a)), and compensation is strictly time-and-materials plus reimbursed expenses as set forth in each SOW (§3(a)-(b)), so fees are payable only for services actually ordered and performed. Targeted searches for "minimum," "commit," "shortfall," "take or pay," "retainer," "non-refundable," and "prepaid" returned no commitment language. On termination, §6(b) entitles Contractor only to "all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned... through the effective date of such termination" — an incurred-cost true-up rather than a penalty or accelerated commitment. Section 3 also contains no minimum hours or guaranteed spend. This satisfies the preferred position, so no redline is proposed. (Noted but out of scope for this rule: §6(a) permits convenience termination only when no uncompleted SOW is outstanding, which is a term/exit point rather than a purchase commitment.)
